units.title: User Rules
units.purpose: Define validation rules and domain constraints for User. Do NOT repeat data isolation (05), lifecycle states (02), or operation flows (03).
units.content: Users must provide a valid email address and a password when signing up. Both email and password are required fields and cannot be empty. Each email address must be unique across the system to prevent duplicate accounts. Users can change their password at any time after logging in. Each user profile requires a display name, which is a required text field. Display names can be updated by the user at any time. When a user deletes their account, all associated data including todos and trash items are permanently removed from the system. The system does not allow email addresses to be changed after account creation.

sections.title: Email Uniqueness Constraint
sections.content: When a user attempts to sign up, the system must verify that the provided email address is not already registered in the system. If the email address matches an existing account, the signup request must be rejected with an appropriate error message indicating that the email is already in use.

sections.title: Password Requirement at Signup
sections.content: THE system SHALL require both an email address and a password when a user signs up for an account. The email field must not be empty, and the password field must not be empty. If either field is missing or blank, the signup request must be rejected.

sections.title: Display Name Requirement
sections.content: THE system SHALL require each user to provide a display name when creating their profile. The display name must not be empty. Users may update their display name at any time after account creation, but the display name can never be left blank.

sections.title: Account Deletion Cascade
sections.content: THE system SHALL permanently delete all associated data when a user deletes their account. This deletion must include all todos created by the user, including todos currently in the trash. The deletion must also include all edit history entries associated with those todos. There must be no way to recover any of this data after account deletion is confirmed.

sections.title: Email Immutability
sections.content: THE system SHALL prevent users from changing their email address after account creation. Once an account is created with an email address, that email address is permanent and immutable. Any attempt to modify the email field must be rejected.

sections.title: Password Change Operation
sections.content: THE system SHALL allow a logged-in user to change their password at any time. The user must provide their current password for verification before a new password can be set. Both the current password and the new password must be non-empty values.

sections.title: User Account Validation Summary
sections.content:
User account validation rules define the constraints for user data integrity.

- Email addresses must be provided during signup and must be unique across the system
- Passwords must be provided during signup and must be non-empty
- Display names must be provided and must be non-empty
- Email addresses cannot be modified after account creation
- Password changes require verification of the current password
- Account deletion results in permanent removal of all associated data

units.title: Todo Rules
units.purpose: Define validation rules and domain constraints for Todo. Do NOT repeat data isolation (05), lifecycle states (02), or operation flows (03).
units.content: Todo items require a title field that cannot be empty when creating or updating. The description field is optional and may be left blank. Start date and due date are both optional date fields that can be set or cleared. When a todo is first created, its completion status defaults to incomplete. The title must contain actual text content; whitespace-only titles are not valid. Todos without a start date are treated as having no start date, which affects sorting behavior. Todos without a due date are treated as having no due date, which affects sorting behavior. Every todo belongs to exactly one user and cannot exist without an owner.

sections.title: Todo Title Requirement
sections.content:
THE system SHALL require that every todo has a non-empty title.

Whitespace-only titles are not valid. A title consisting only of spaces, tabs, or other whitespace characters shall be rejected as invalid.

When validating a title, the system SHALL trim leading and trailing whitespace before checking whether content exists.

If a user attempts to create or update a todo without providing a valid title, the system SHALL reject the request and report that a title is required.

sections.title: Description Field Optionality
sections.content:
THE system SHALL treat the description field as optional.

Users MAY provide a description when creating or editing a todo. Users MAY also leave the description empty or blank.

An empty description is a valid state and shall be stored without error.

When viewing a todo with an empty description, the system SHALL display an empty description area rather than indicating an error.

sections.title: Start Date Optionality
sections.content:
THE system SHALL treat the start date field as optional.

Users MAY provide a start date when creating or editing a todo. Users MAY also leave the start date unset.

When the start date is not set, the system SHALL treat the todo as having no start date.

If a user clears an existing start date, the system SHALL accept this change and the todo shall have no start date thereafter.

sections.title: Due Date Optionality
sections.content:
THE system SHALL treat the due date field as optional.

Users MAY provide a due date when creating or editing a todo. Users MAY also leave the due date unset.

When the due date is not set, the system SHALL treat the todo as having no due date.

If a user clears an existing due date, the system SHALL accept this change and the todo shall have no due date thereafter.

sections.title: Default Completion Status
sections.content:
THE system SHALL set the completion status to incomplete when a todo is first created.

A newly created todo shall always start in the incomplete state, regardless of what other fields are set.

The completion status can be changed later through explicit complete or incomplete actions initiated by the user.

sections.title: Todo Ownership Requirement
sections.content:
THE system SHALL require that every todo has an owner.

A todo cannot exist without being associated with a user account. The owner is set automatically when the todo is created and cannot be changed afterwards.

Users can only create todos that belong to their own account. A user cannot create a todo on behalf of another user.

When a user account is deleted, all todos owned by that user are permanently deleted as well.

sections.title: Sorting Behavior for Todos Without Start Date
sections.content:
WHEN sorting todos by start date in ascending order, THE system SHALL place todos without a start date after all todos that have a start date.

WHEN sorting todos by start date in descending order, THE system SHALL place todos without a start date after all todos that have a start date.

Todos without a start date shall always appear at the end of the sorted list, regardless of sort direction.

sections.title: Sorting Behavior for Todos Without Due Date
sections.content:
WHEN sorting todos by due date in ascending order, THE system SHALL place todos without a due date after all todos that have a due date.

WHEN sorting todos by due date in descending order, THE system SHALL place todos without a due date after all todos that have a due date.

Todos without a due date shall always appear at the end of the sorted list, regardless of sort direction.

units.title: TodoEditHistory Rules
units.purpose: Define validation rules and domain constraints for TodoEditHistory. Do NOT repeat data isolation (05), lifecycle states (02), or operation flows (03).
units.content: Edit history entries are created automatically whenever a todo is modified by its owner. Each history entry records the timestamp when the edit occurred. A history entry may contain a title value if the title was changed during that edit; if the title was not changed, the title field in the history entry is not recorded. Similarly, description changes are recorded only when the description value differs from its previous state. Start date changes are captured in history only when the start date was modified. Due date changes are captured in history only when the due date was modified. History entries are immutable once created and cannot be modified or deleted by users. When a todo is permanently deleted from trash, all associated history entries are also permanently deleted.
keywords: history deletion on permanent todo deletion

sections.title: History Entry Creation
sections.content:
WHEN a user edits a todo that they own, THEN the system SHALL automatically create a history entry to record the edit.

WHEN a user saves changes to a todo title, description, start date, or due date, THEN a history entry SHALL be created capturing the state of those fields at the time of the edit.

WHEN a user edits a todo but makes no actual changes to any field, THEN no history entry SHALL be created.

WHEN a todo is created, THEN no initial history entry SHALL be created.

sections.title: Timestamp Recording
sections.content:
EACH history entry SHALL record the exact date and time when the edit was made.

The timestamp SHALL represent when the user saved the edit, not when the edit began.

History entries SHALL be sortable by their timestamp in descending order (most recent first).

sections.title: Title Change Recording
sections.content:
IF the todo title was changed during an edit, THEN the history entry SHALL record the new title value.

IF the todo title was not changed during an edit, THEN the history entry SHALL NOT record a title value for that field.

WHEN a title change is recorded, the history entry SHALL store the complete title as it existed after the edit was saved.

sections.title: Description Change Recording
sections.content:
IF the todo description was changed during an edit, THEN the history entry SHALL record the new description value.

IF the todo description was not changed during an edit, THEN the history entry SHALL NOT record a description value for that field.

IF the user cleared a description that previously had content, this SHALL be treated as a change and SHALL be recorded.

sections.title: Start Date Change Recording
sections.content:
IF the todo start date was changed during an edit, THEN the history entry SHALL record the new start date value.

IF the todo start date was not changed during an edit, THEN the history entry SHALL NOT record a start date value for that field.

IF the user removed a start date that was previously set, this SHALL be treated as a change and SHALL be recorded.

IF the user set a start date where none was previously set, this SHALL be treated as a change and SHALL be recorded.

sections.title: Due Date Change Recording
sections.content:
IF the todo due date was changed during an edit, THEN the history entry SHALL record the new due date value.

IF the todo due date was not changed during an edit, THEN the history entry SHALL NOT record a due date value for that field.

IF the user removed a due date that was previously set, this SHALL be treated as a change and SHALL be recorded.

IF the user set a due date where none was previously set, this SHALL be treated as a change and SHALL be recorded.

sections.title: History Entry Immutability
sections.content:
ONCE a history entry is created, it SHALL be immutable and SHALL NOT be modified.

Users SHALL NOT be able to edit, delete, or otherwise modify any history entry.

System administrators SHALL NOT be able to manually alter history entries.

The immutability of history entries ensures the integrity of the edit audit trail.

sections.title: History Deletion on Permanent Todo Deletion
sections.content:
WHEN a todo is permanently deleted from the trash, THEN all associated history entries for that todo SHALL be permanently deleted.

The deletion of history entries SHALL occur atomically with the todo deletion.

There SHALL be no ability to restore history entries after a permanent deletion.

IF a todo is restored from trash, its history entries SHALL also be restored with it.

sections.title: History Access and Visibility
sections.content:
USERS SHALL be able to view the full edit history of any todo they own.

USERS SHALL NOT be able to view the edit history of todos owned by other users.

The edit history SHALL display entries sorted from most recent to oldest.

Each history entry SHALL clearly show which fields were changed in that edit.

units.title: List Browsing Expectations
units.purpose: Define business expectations for how users find, filter, and browse lists.
units.content: Define business expectations for how users find, filter, and browse lists.

sections.title: Filtering by Completion Status
sections.content:
Users can apply filters to their todo list to narrow down displayed results based on specific criteria.

When a user selects a completion status filter, the system displays only todos matching that filter. The available filter options are:

- All todos: displays every todo belonging to the user
- Only complete todos: displays todos that have been marked as complete
- Only incomplete todos: displays todos that have not been marked as complete

The filter applies to the current view (either the normal todo list or the trash view). When the user changes the filter, the list updates to show only todos matching the selected criteria.

The current filter selection persists until the user changes it or logs out.

sections.title: Sorting Options
sections.content:
Users can change the order in which their todos are displayed by selecting a sorting option.

The available sorting options are:

- Creation date, newest first: todos appear with the most recently created at the top
- Creation date, oldest first: todos appear with the earliest created at the top
- Start date, earliest first: todos appear with the earliest start date at the top
- Start date, latest first: todos appear with the most recent start date at the top
- Due date, earliest first: todos appear with the soonest due date at the top
- Due date, latest first: todos appear with the furthest due date at the top

When sorting by start date, todos that do not have a start date assigned appear at the end of the list regardless of sort direction.

When sorting by due date, todos that do not have a due date assigned appear at the end of the list regardless of sort direction.

The current sort selection persists until the user changes it or logs out.

sections.title: Pagination of Lists
sections.content:
The system presents todo lists in segments to avoid overwhelming users with large amounts of data.

When viewing the todo list or the trash list, the system displays a subset of todos along with navigation controls to access additional segments.

Users can navigate between segments using previous and next controls when available. The system indicates the current position within the total set of todos.

Pagination applies independently to the normal todo list and the trash list. Changing pages in one view does not affect the other.

When filters or sorting options are changed, the list returns to the first segment.

units.title: Error Scenarios
units.purpose: Describe error conditions and expected system responses in natural language.
units.content: Describe error conditions and expected system responses in natural language.

sections.title: Todo Not Found Error
sections.content:
When a user attempts to perform an operation on a todo that does not exist, the system must reject the request and return an appropriate error message indicating the todo could not be found.

**Examples of this error scenario:**
- Attempting to view details of a todo using an identifier that does not correspond to any existing todo
- Attempting to edit a todo that has been permanently deleted
- Attempting to complete or delete a todo that was never created

The system must not reveal whether the identifier format is valid or if the todo existed before, to prevent enumeration attacks.

sections.title: Unauthorized Todo Access Error
sections.content:
When a user attempts to access, view, modify, or delete a todo that belongs to another user, the system must reject the request and return an error message indicating access is denied.

**Examples of this error scenario:**
- Attempting to view the details of another user's todo
- Attempting to edit the title, description, or dates of another user's todo
- Attempting to mark another user's todo as complete or incomplete
- Attempting to delete another user's todo
- Attempting to view the edit history of another user's todo
- Attempting to restore or permanently delete another user's todo from the trash

The system must not provide any indication that the requested todo exists or belonged to another user.

sections.title: Unauthenticated Access Error
sections.content:
When a user attempts to perform an operation that requires authentication while being unauthenticated, the system must reject the request and return an error message indicating authentication is required.

**Examples of this error scenario:**
- Attempting to create a todo without being logged in
- Attempting to view the todo list without being logged in
- Attempting to edit a todo without being logged in
- Attempting to delete a todo without being logged in
- Attempting to access the trash without being logged in
- Attempting to restore a todo without being logged in

sections.title: Missing Todo Title Error
sections.content:
When a user attempts to create a new todo without providing a title, the system must reject the request and return an error message indicating that a title is required.

**This error applies only to todo creation.** Edits to existing todos do not require any specific field to be provided.

sections.title: Invalid Date Range Error
sections.content:
When a user attempts to set a due date on a todo that is earlier than the start date, the system must reject the request and return an error message indicating that the due date cannot be earlier than the start date.

**Examples of this error scenario:**
- Setting a due date to yesterday while the start date is today
- Setting a start date to next week while the due date is this week

This validation applies to both creating a new todo and editing an existing todo.

sections.title: Permanently Deleted Todo Error
sections.content:
When a user attempts to access, modify, or delete a todo that has been permanently deleted from the trash, the system must reject the request and return an error message indicating the todo could not be found.

**Examples of this error scenario:**
- Attempting to view the details of a permanently deleted todo
- Attempting to edit a permanently deleted todo
- Attempting to complete or uncomplete a permanently deleted todo
- Attempting to view the edit history of a permanently deleted todo

Permanently deleted todos and their associated edit history are removed from the system and cannot be recovered or accessed.

sections.title: Todo Not Found in Trash Error
sections.content:
When a user attempts to restore a todo from the trash that has already been permanently deleted, the system must reject the request and return an error message indicating the todo could not be found in the trash.

**This error scenario is distinct from the general "todo not found" error** because it specifically relates to the trash view where users expect to find their deleted items.

sections.title: Invalid Operation for Current State Error
sections.content:
When a user attempts to perform an operation that is not valid for a todo in its current state, the system must reject the request and return an appropriate error message.

**Examples of this error scenario:**
- Attempting to restore a todo that is not currently in the trash (it has already been restored or was never deleted)
- Attempting to move a todo to the trash when it is already in the trash

The system must validate state transitions before executing any operation.

sections.title: System Failure Handling
sections.content:
When the system encounters an unexpected error while processing a user request, it must handle the situation gracefully and return a generic error message to the user without exposing internal details.

**Examples of this failure case:**
- Database connection failure during a save operation
- Unexpected data corruption detected during retrieval
- System resource exhaustion during processing

The system must log detailed error information for debugging purposes while presenting users with a user-friendly message indicating something went wrong and suggesting they try again later.

files.content:
**multiUserTodo — Data ownership, privacy, retention, and recovery policies**

Data ownership, privacy, retention, and recovery policies

# Data Policies

Data ownership, privacy, retention, and recovery policies from a business perspective.

## Data Ownership and Privacy

Define who owns what data, who can access it, and privacy boundaries between users.

### Data Ownership Principles

Every user owns the data they create within the application. When a user creates a todo, that todo belongs exclusively to that user. The user who creates a todo is its sole owner and retains full control over it throughout its lifecycle.

Ownership extends to all associated data, including edit history entries. Each edit history entry belongs to the todo it records changes for, and indirectly to the user who owns that todo.

A user cannot acquire ownership of todos created by another user under any circumstances. Ownership is permanent and cannot be transferred, shared, or assigned to another user.

### Data Isolation Between Users

Each user's data is completely isolated from all other users. A user can only access their own data and has no ability to view, retrieve, or interact with any data belonging to another user.

This isolation applies to all data types including todos, edit history entries, and user profile information.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph UserA["User A"]
        A1["Todo 1"]
        A2["Todo 2"]
        A3["History A1"]
    end
    subgraph UserB["User B"]
        B1["Todo 3"]
        B2["Todo 4"]
        B3["History B1"]
    end
    A1 -->|Can access| A1
    B1 -->|Can access| B1
    A1 -.->|Cannot access| B1
    B1 -.->|Cannot access| A1
```

The system enforces isolation at the data level, ensuring that no user can bypass boundaries through any available operation.

### Access Control Boundaries

Access to data is strictly limited to the user who owns it. There are no exceptions, no shared access modes, and no administrative overrides that allow one user to view another user's data.

The system enforces access control through the following principles:

- **Self-only access**: Users can only access their own todos, their own edit history entries, and their own profile
- **No cross-user queries**: The system does not provide any mechanism to list, search, or retrieve todos belonging to other users
- **No sharing**: There is no sharing functionality that allows users to grant access to their todos to any other user
- **Private by default**: All todos are private and hidden from all other users by default

These access controls apply regardless of the data's state. A todo in trash remains private and inaccessible to other users.

### Privacy Guarantees

Privacy is a fundamental property of the application. Each user's todos, including their titles, descriptions, dates, and completion status, are completely private.

The application does not expose any user data to other users. This means:

- Users cannot discover that another user exists through the application
- Users cannot see the number of todos owned by another user
- Users cannot view, preview, or reference another user's todos through any interface or API
- User profile information, including display name, is not visible to other users

The privacy boundary is absolute and cannot be crossed through normal application usage or through any administrative function provided to users.

### Data Privacy Upon Account Deletion

When a user deletes their account, all associated data is permanently removed from the system. This includes:

- All todos created by the user, including those in the trash
- All edit history entries associated with those todos
- The user's profile information

This deletion is irreversible. Once an account is deleted, no portion of the user's data remains accessible to anyone, including the deleted user themselves.

### User Control Over Their Data

Users have full control over the lifecycle of their own data. Users can:

- Create todos that belong to them
- Delete todos, moving them to trash
- Restore deleted todos from trash
- Permanently delete todos from trash
- Edit their profile information
- Delete their account and all associated data

The system does not retain, archive, or backup user data beyond what is necessary for the application to function. When data is permanently deleted, it is removed from all storage locations.

## Data Retention and Recovery

Define what happens to deleted data, how long it is retained, and how users can recover it.

### Soft Delete Policy

When a user deletes a todo, the system performs a soft_delete. Soft delete means the todo is marked as deleted but the data remains in the system.

Deleted todos are removed from the user's normal todo list and are no longer visible among active todos. The system retains all todo data including title, description, start date, due date, completion status, and creation date.

The soft_delete operation preserves the entire edit history associated with the todo. This allows users to review what changes were made to a todo even after it has been deleted.

Soft deleted todos remain recoverable until the user permanently deletes them.

### Trash Retention

Deleted todos are stored in the trash. The trash serves as an intermediate holding area between active use and permanent deletion.

Users can view all their deleted todos in the trash list. The trash list is paginated, matching the pagination behavior of the normal todo list.

There is no automatic cleanup of the trash. Todos remain in the trash indefinitely until the user takes action to either restore or permanently delete them.

When a todo is in the trash, users can still view its full details including all edit history entries.

### Todo Recovery

Users can restore a deleted todo from the trash. When restored, the todo returns to the normal todo list with all its data intact.

The restored todo maintains its original title, description, start date, due date, and completion status. The edit history is preserved and remains accessible.

Restoring a todo does not modify any existing edit history entries. The restoration itself is not recorded as an edit in the history.

After restoration, the todo no longer appears in the trash.

### Permanent Deletion

Users can permanently delete a todo from the trash. Permanent deletion removes all data associated with the todo from the system.

When a todo is permanently deleted, the system deletes the todo itself and all associated edit history entries. This action cannot be undone.

The permanent deletion operation is irreversible. There is no recovery mechanism for permanently deleted todos.

After permanent deletion, the todo no longer appears in the trash and is not accessible through any system view.

### Account Deletion and Data Removal

When a user deletes their account, all associated data is permanently removed from the system. This includes all active todos, all todos in the trash, and all edit history entries.

Account deletion is an irreversible action. There is no recovery mechanism for deleted accounts or their associated data.

The system does not retain any data belonging to a deleted user account.

# Designing Database Schema

The requirements analysis is complete. Now I'll execute the **Database Agent** to generate the database schema and ERD documentation based on the structured specification.

**What I found from requirements:**

| Entity | Key Attributes |
|--------|----------------|
| **User** | id, email, password, displayName, createdAt, updatedAt |
| **Todo** | id, userId, title, description, startDate, dueDate, isComplete, deletedAt, createdAt, updatedAt |

instruction:
Create a database schema for a multi-user Todo application with the following requirements:

## User Account
- Users sign up with email and password
- Users log in with email and password
- Users can change their password
- Users can delete their account (all their todos, including those in trash, are permanently deleted)

## User Profile
- Each user has a profile with: display name
- Users can edit their display name

## Creating Todos
- Users can create a todo with:
  - Title (required)
  - Description (optional, can be left empty)
  - Start date (optional, can be left empty)
  - Due date (optional, can be left empty)
- Newly created todos are incomplete by default

## Viewing Todos
- Users can view a list of their own todos
- The list is paginated
- Each todo in the list shows: title, completion status, start date (if set), due date (if set), and creation date
- Users can view a single todo to see all its details including full description

## Completing Todos
- Users can mark a todo as complete
- Users can mark a todo as incomplete
- This is a simple toggle between two states

## Editing Todos
- Users can edit their todo's title, description, start date, and due date
- Every edit is recorded in the todo's history

## Edit History
- Each todo has an edit history
- Every time a todo is edited, a history entry is created
- Each history entry records:
  - When the edit was made
  - What the title was changed to (if changed)
  - What the description was changed to (if changed)
  - What the start date was changed to (if changed)
  - What the due date was changed to (if changed)
- Users can view the full edit history of any of their todos
- History entries are sorted from most recent to oldest

## Deleting Todos
- Users can delete their own todos
- Deleted todos are not permanently removed (soft delete)
- Deleted todos no longer appear in the normal todo list

## Trash
- Users can view a list of their deleted todos (trash)
- The trash list is paginated
- Users can restore a deleted todo from the trash (it returns to the normal todo list)
- Users can permanently delete a todo from the trash
- Permanently deleting a todo also deletes its edit history

## Privacy
- Each user's todos are completely private
- Users can only see their own todos

models.name: multi_user_todo_guests

models.name: multi_user_todo_guest_sessions
models.description:
Temporary session tokens for guest access, tracking anonymous user sessions.

This table stores session information for unauthenticated visitors (guests) before they register or log in. Each session is linked to a guest via the multi_user_todo_guest_id foreign key. The table tracks connection metadata including IP address, request URL (href), and referrer for analytics and security purposes. Sessions expire based on the expired_at timestamp and are not soft-deleted since they naturally expire.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP referrer header value indicating the previous page.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expires and becomes invalid.

plainFields.name: updated_at

models.name: multi_user_todo_todos
models.description:
Main todo items owned by users with title, description, dates, completion status, and soft-delete support via deleted_at timestamp for trash workflow.

foreignFields.description: Owner's member ID. References {@link multi_user_todo_members.id} for privacy isolation - each user can only see their own todos.

plainFields.description: Todo title - the main task description. Required on creation.

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description: Optional start date for the todo. Null if not set.

plainFields.name: due_date
plainFields.description: Optional due date for the todo. Null if not set.

plainFields.name: completed
plainFields.description: Completion status flag. False by default when todo is created.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-delete timestamp. Null means not deleted. When set, todo is in trash and excluded from normal list.

### `multi_user_todo_guests`

Temporary guest accounts for unauthenticated visitors identified by
device ID before registration or login. Guests are anonymous users
tracked by their device identifier, allowing the system to maintain
context for unauthenticated users until they choose to register or log
in.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `device_id`
  > Unique device identifier used to track anonymous guest users. This allows
  > the system to maintain session continuity for unauthenticated visitors
  > identified by their device.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the guest account was first created. Records when this
  > device was first seen by the system.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the guest account was last updated. Tracks the last
  > activity or modification time for this guest record.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the guest account was soft deleted. Null means the guest
  > account is active. Used for cleanup of stale or converted guest records.

### `multi_user_todo_guest_sessions`

Temporary session tokens for guest access, tracking anonymous user sessions.

This table stores session information for unauthenticated visitors
(guests) before they register or log in. Each session is linked to a
guest via the multi_user_todo_guest_id foreign key. The table tracks
connection metadata including IP address, request URL (href), and
referrer for analytics and security purposes. Sessions expire based on
the expired_at timestamp and are not soft-deleted since they naturally
expire.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `multi_user_todo_guest_id`
  > Associated guest's [multi_user_todo_guests.id](#multi_user_todo_guests). This links the
  > session to the guest who owns it.
- `ip`: IP address of the client making the request.
- `href`: Requested URL path for this session.
- `referrer`: HTTP referrer header value indicating the previous page.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the session was created.
- `expired_at`: Timestamp when the session expires and becomes invalid.

### `multi_user_todo_members`

Registered user accounts with email and password authentication
credentials for authenticated access. This is the primary actor table
representing authenticated members who can create, manage, and delete
their own todos. Each member has a profile with display name that can be
edited. Account deletion is permanent and cascades to all associated
todos.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`
  > Unique email address used for login authentication and account
  > identification.
- `password_hash`: Bcrypt hashed password for secure authentication.
- `display_name`
  > Public display name shown in the member's profile and around the
  > application.
- `created_at`: When the member account was created.
- `updated_at`: When the member account was last updated.

### `multi_user_todo_member_sessions`

JWT session tokens for maintaining authenticated member sessions with
access and refresh token support. Each session records the member's login
event including connection metadata (IP address, URL, referrer) and JWT
token pair. Sessions are created upon successful login and tracked until
expiration. Multiple concurrent sessions per member are supported.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `multi_user_todo_member_id`
  > Authenticated member who owns this session. {@link
  > multi_user_todo_members.id}.
- `access_token`: JWT access token for authenticated API requests.
- `refresh_token`: JWT refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.
- `ip`: Client IP address at session creation.
- `href`: Current request URL path.
- `referrer`: HTTP referrer header value.
- `created_at`: Session creation timestamp.
- `expired_at`: Session expiration timestamp. NOT NULL to enforce mandatory expiration.

### `multi_user_todo_member_password_resets`

Password reset tokens for member account recovery and password change
flows. Each token has an expiration time and can be marked as used.
Managed through authentication processes, not direct user operations.
[multi_user_todo_members](#multi_user_todo_members) owns many password reset tokens.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `multi_user_todo_member_id`
  > The member who requested this password reset. {@link
  > multi_user_todo_members.id}.
- `token_hash`: Hashed password reset token for security. Never store plaintext tokens.
- `expired_at`
  > Expiration timestamp for this reset token. Token is invalid after this
  > time.
- `used_at`: Timestamp when this reset token was used. Null if not yet used.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this password reset was requested.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of the last update to this record.

### `multi_user_todo_member_email_verifications`

Email verification tokens for member account registration verification.
Each record stores a unique verification token sent to the member's email
during registration. Tokens have expiration times and are marked as
verified when the member confirms their email address through the
verification link.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `multi_user_todo_member_id`
  > Belonged member's [multi_user_todo_members.id](#multi_user_todo_members). This is the member
  > account this verification token belongs to.
- `token`
  > Unique verification token string sent to the member's email. Used as the
  > lookup key during email verification.
- `expires_at`
  > Expiration timestamp for the verification token. Tokens become invalid
  > after this time.
- `verified_at`: Timestamp when the verification was completed. Null if not yet verified.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the verification token was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the verification token was last updated.

### `multi_user_todo_todos`

Main todo items owned by users with title, description, dates, completion
status, and soft-delete support via deleted_at timestamp for trash
workflow.

Each todo belongs to exactly one member and captures task management data
including optional start/due dates and completion status. The soft-delete
pattern enables the trash workflow where users can view deleted todos,
restore them, or permanently delete them.

Relationships:
- Owned by [multi_user_todo_members](#multi_user_todo_members) via multi_user_todo_member_id
FK for privacy isolation
- Has many [multi_user_todo_todo_edit_histories](#multi_user_todo_todo_edit_histories) entries recording
all field mutations

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `multi_user_todo_member_id`
  > Owner's member ID. References [multi_user_todo_members.id](#multi_user_todo_members) for
  > privacy isolation - each user can only see their own todos.
- `title`: Todo title - the main task description. Required on creation.
- `description`: Optional detailed description of the todo. Can be empty string.
- `start_date`: Optional start date for the todo. Null if not set.
- `due_date`: Optional due date for the todo. Null if not set.
- `completed`: Completion status flag. False by default when todo is created.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the todo was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the todo was last modified.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft-delete timestamp. Null means not deleted. When set, todo is in trash
  > and excluded from normal list.

### `multi_user_todo_todo_edit_histories`

Edit history entries recording field-level mutations for todo items. Each
entry captures old and new values for title, description, start_date, and
due_date when a todo is edited, with a timestamp. History entries are
created automatically when todos are edited and cannot be modified or
deleted independently by users.

- `id`: Primary Key.

  > this edit.

  > Previous description value before this edit. Null if description was not
  > changed in this edit.

  > changed in this edit.

  > changed in this edit.
- `new_start_date`
  > New start date value after this edit. Null if start date was not changed
  > in this edit.
- `old_due_date`
  > Previous due date value before this edit. Null if due date was not
  > changed in this edit.
- `new_due_date`
  > New due date value after this edit. Null if due date was not changed in
  > this edit.

The database schema is complete. Now I'll execute the **Interface Agent** to design and generate the API interfaces with OpenAPI schemas.

**Completed Steps:**

instruction:
Design and create API interfaces for a multi-user Todo application with the following specifications:

## Authentication Endpoints
- POST /auth/signup - Register new user with email and password
- POST /auth/login - Login with email and password
- POST /auth/change-password - Change password (authenticated)
- DELETE /auth/account - Delete account and all associated data (authenticated)

## User Profile Endpoints
- GET /users/me - Get current user profile
- PATCH /users/me - Update display name

## Todo Endpoints
- GET /todos - List user's todos with pagination
  - Query params: page, limit, status (all|complete|incomplete), sortBy (createdAt|startDate|dueDate), sortOrder (asc|desc)
- POST /todos - Create new todo
  - Body: title (required), description, startDate, dueDate
- GET /todos/:id - Get single todo with full details
- PATCH /todos/:id - Update todo
  - Body: title, description, startDate, dueDate
- POST /todos/:id/toggle - Toggle completion status
- DELETE /todos/:id - Soft delete todo (move to trash)
- POST /todos/:id/restore - Restore todo from trash

## Todo History Endpoints
- GET /todos/:id/history - Get edit history for a todo (sorted newest first)

## Trash Endpoints
- GET /trash - List deleted todos (paginated)
- DELETE /trash/:id - Permanently delete todo from trash
- DELETE /trash - Empty trash (delete all todos in trash)

## Filtering Requirements
- Filter todos by completion status: all, complete, or incomplete

## Sorting Requirements
- Sort by: createdAt, startDate, dueDate
- Sort order: asc or desc
- Null handling: todos without startDate/dueDate appear at end when sorting by those fields

## Pagination
- All list endpoints are paginated
- Default page: 1, default limit: 20
- Response includes: items, total, page, limit, totalPages

## Privacy
- All endpoints are authenticated
- Users can only access their own data

operations.specification:
1. Extract device_id from request body
2. Validate device_id is not empty and is a valid UUID format
3. Check if guest with this device_id already exists (by device_id unique constraint)
4. If exists and not deleted, return existing guest record
5. If exists and soft-deleted, restore the guest (clear deleted_at, update updated_at)
6. If not exists, create new guest record with generated UUID and current timestamps
7. Generate JWT access token with guest ID, expiry (typically 15-30 minutes)
8. Generate JWT refresh token with guest ID, expiry (typically 7-30 days)
9. Store refresh token in multi_user_todo_guest_sessions table with client metadata (ip, href, referrer, expired_at)
10. Return access token and refresh token in response
operations.description:
Guest user registration endpoint that creates a new guest account or restores an existing one based on device identifier.

This operation handles unauthenticated visitor registration using device_id as the primary identification mechanism. The device_id field from the multi_user_todo_guests table uniquely identifies the guest device, allowing the system to maintain session continuity for anonymous users before they register or log in.

Security considerations include validating the device_id format, preventing duplicate registrations for the same device, and generating secure JWT tokens with appropriate expiration times. The session tracking captures client metadata (IP address, request URL, referrer) for analytics and security audit purposes.

The multi_user_todo_guest_sessions table stores session information linked to the guest via multi_user_todo_guest_id foreign key. Sessions track connection metadata including IP address (ip field), requested URL path (href field), HTTP referrer header (referrer field), creation timestamp (created_at), and expiration timestamp (expired_at).

Related operations include the refresh endpoint for renewing expired tokens using the refresh token flow.

Request validation: device_id must be a non-empty string, properly formatted UUID or device identifier. Response includes access_token for API authentication and refresh_token for token renewal.

requestBody.description: Request body containing guest registration information including device identifier for session tracking.

responseBody.description: Response containing authentication tokens for the registered guest user.

operations.name: join

operations.specification:
1. Extract refresh_token from request body
2. Validate refresh_token format and signature (JWT validation)
3. Check if refresh_token exists in multi_user_todo_guest_sessions table and is not expired
4. Verify session's expired_at is greater than current timestamp
5. If session is valid, retrieve associated multi_user_todo_guest_id
6. Verify guest exists in multi_user_todo_guests table and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null)
7. Generate new JWT access token with guest ID and new expiry
8. Optionally generate new refresh token (token rotation) or reuse same refresh token
9. Update session record's expired_at timestamp if new refresh token is issued
10. Return new access token and optionally new refresh token in response
operations.description:
Token refresh endpoint that renews expired or expiring access tokens using a valid refresh token.

This operation allows guest users to maintain their authenticated session without re-registering. The refresh token workflow uses the multi_user_todo_guest_sessions table which stores session information with expiration timestamps (expired_at field). Sessions are linked to guests via the multi_user_todo_guest_id foreign key.

Security considerations include validating token signatures, checking token expiration against the expired_at timestamp, ensuring the associated guest account is not soft-deleted (deleted_at must be null in multi_user_todo_guests table), and optionally implementing token rotation for enhanced security.

The session tracking captures client metadata including IP address (ip), requested URL (href), and HTTP referrer (referrer) from the original session creation. This metadata remains associated with the refreshed session.

Related operations include the join endpoint for initial guest registration that creates the refresh token.

Request validation: refresh_token must be a valid JWT string. Response includes new access_token and optionally new refresh_token.

requestBody.description: Request body containing the refresh token for token renewal.

responseBody.description: Response containing new authentication tokens after successful refresh.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: 1. Validate the email field (must be valid email format, must be unique per the members table's @@unique([email]) constraint). 2. Validate the password field (must meet system password requirements). 3. Hash the password using bcrypt with appropriate cost factor. 4. Generate a new UUID for the member's id field. 5. Insert a new record into the multi_user_todo_members table with email, password_hash, and display_name. 6. Generate JWT access_token and refresh_token for the new member. 7. Create a new session record in multi_user_todo_member_sessions with the tokens, client metadata (IP, href, referrer), and expiration timestamp. 8. Return the tokens and member information in the IAuthorized response format.
operations.description:
Creates a new member account for user registration.

This endpoint allows unauthenticated users (guests) to create a new registered member account by providing their email address, password, and display name. The email must be unique across the system as enforced by the unique constraint on the email field in the multi_user_todo_members database table. Upon successful registration, the system creates a new member record with a bcrypt-hashed password, generates JWT access and refresh tokens, establishes a new session in the multi_user_todo_member_sessions table, and returns the authentication tokens along with basic member information.

The registration process validates that the email address is not already associated with an existing account before creating the new member. The password is securely hashed using bcrypt before storage. A new session record is created linking the member to their initial authentication session with client metadata (IP address, request URL, and HTTP referrer).

This operation transitions a guest to an authenticated member with full access to the todo management system. The returned access token should be used in the Authorization header for subsequent authenticated API requests.

requestBody.description: Registration request containing email, password, and display name for new member account creation.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and member information returned upon successful registration.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: 1. Validate the email field exists and is a valid email format. 2. Validate the password field is not empty. 3. Query the multi_user_todo_members table to find a record matching the provided email. 4. Verify the provided password matches the stored password_hash using bcrypt comparison. 5. If credentials are invalid, return an authentication error. 6. Generate new JWT access_token and refresh_token for the authenticated member. 7. Create a new session record in multi_user_todo_member_sessions with the tokens, client metadata (IP, href, referrer), and expiration timestamp. 8. Return the tokens and member information in the IAuthorized response format.
operations.description:
Authenticates an existing member with email and password credentials.

This endpoint performs credential validation for registered members who wish to log into the system. The member provides their registered email address and password. The system looks up the email in the multi_user_todo_members table (enforcing the unique email constraint), retrieves the stored bcrypt password hash, and verifies the provided password matches. If authentication succeeds, the system generates new JWT access and refresh tokens, creates a session record in the multi_user_todo_member_sessions table with client metadata (IP address, request URL, and HTTP referrer), and returns the authentication tokens.

Failed login attempts (invalid email or incorrect password) return an authentication error without revealing which field was incorrect. The system supports multiple concurrent sessions per member, allowing users to be logged in from multiple devices simultaneously.

Upon successful login, the returned access token should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent authenticated API requests. The refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens when the current one expires.

requestBody.description: Login request containing email and password credentials for member authentication.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and member information returned upon successful login.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: 1. Validate the refresh_token field exists and is not empty. 2. Verify the JWT refresh token is valid and not expired by checking the signature and expiration. 3. Extract the member ID from the refresh token payload. 4. Query the multi_user_todo_member_sessions table to verify the session exists and is associated with the member. 5. Check that the session has not expired (expired_at > current timestamp). 6. Generate a new access_token (and optionally a new refresh_token). 7. Update the session record with the new tokens and potentially new expiration timestamp. 8. Return the new tokens and member information in the IAuthorized response format.
operations.description:
Refreshes authentication tokens using a valid refresh token.

This endpoint allows members to obtain new access tokens without re-authenticating with their email and password. The client provides a valid refresh_token that was issued during login or a previous refresh operation. The system validates the JWT refresh token signature, checks that it has not expired, verifies the associated session exists in the multi_user_todo_member_sessions table, and confirms the session has not passed its expiration timestamp.

Upon successful validation, the system generates a new access token (and may optionally generate a new refresh token) and updates the session record with the fresh tokens. The old refresh token is invalidated and replaced with the new one for security. The returned access token should be used for subsequent authenticated API requests.

This mechanism enables long-lived authenticated sessions without requiring users to repeatedly enter their credentials. When the new access token expires, the client can use the new refresh token to obtain another access token.

responseBody.description: New authentication tokens and member information returned upon successful token refresh.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of todos owned by the authenticated member.

This endpoint provides comprehensive todo listing with support for filtering by completion status, sorting by creation date or due dates, and cursor-based pagination for efficient browsing of large todo collections.

The operation enforces strict ownership isolation - members can only see their own todos. Todos that have been soft-deleted (moved to trash) are excluded from the normal listing and can only be accessed through the trash endpoint.

Filtering Options:
- By completion status: all, complete, or incomplete todos
- By date ranges if needed

Sorting Options:
- By creation date (createdAt)
- By start date (startDate) - todos without start date appear at end
- By due date (dueDate) - todos without due date appear at end

The response includes summary information optimized for list displays, showing title, completion status, dates, and item count. For full todo details, use GET /todos/{todoId}.

Related Operations:
- GET /todos/{todoId} - Retrieve full todo details
- POST /todos - Create a new todo
- PATCH /todos/{todoId} - Update todo fields
- POST /todos/{todoId}/toggle - Toggle completion status
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query multi_user_todo_todos table filtering by owner_id from authenticated session.

Apply the following filters from request body:
- status filter: 'complete' (where completed_at IS NOT NULL), 'incomplete' (where completed_at IS NULL), or 'all' (no filter)
- date range filters if provided (startDateFrom, startDateTo, dueDateFrom, dueDateTo)

Apply sorting based on sortBy parameter:
- 'createdAt': ORDER BY created_at [sortOrder]
- 'startDate': ORDER BY start_date [sortOrder] NULLS LAST
- 'dueDate': ORDER BY due_date [sortOrder] NULLS LAST

Implement pagination:
- Skip (page - 1) * limit records
- Return limit records
- Include total count for pagination metadata

Exclude soft-deleted todos (WHERE deleted_at IS NULL) from normal listing.

Return IPageIMultiUserTodoTodo.ISummary array with pagination metadata.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of todo summaries with pagination metadata

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific todo item by its unique identifier.

This endpoint returns the complete details of a single todo including its title, description, start date, due date, completion status, and timestamps. The operation enforces strict ownership verification - only todos belonging to the authenticated member can be retrieved.

Security: This operation requires authentication. The system validates that the requested todo belongs to the requesting user by comparing the todo's multi_user_todo_member_id with the authenticated user's ID. Attempting to access another user's todo will result in a not found error for security reasons (preventing enumeration attacks).

Database relationships: The todo references the multi_user_todo_members table via multi_user_todo_member_id foreign key for ownership verification. Each todo may have associated edit history entries in the todo_edit_histories table.

Response format: Returns the full todo object with all fields including nullable fields (description may be empty string, start_date and due_date may be null if not set).

Error handling: If the todo does not exist or does not belong to the authenticated user, return a 404 error with a generic message indicating the resource could not be found.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
1. Extract todoId from path parameters
2. Authenticate the requesting member via session token
3. Query the database: SELECT * FROM multi_user_todo_todos WHERE id = todoId AND multi_user_todo_member_id = authenticated_user_id AND deleted_at IS NULL
4. If not found or belongs to different user, return 404 error with generic message
5. If found, return the complete todo object with all fields
6. Do not include soft-deleted todos (deleted_at IS NOT NULL)

responseBody.description: Complete todo object with all fields

operations.description:
Create a new todo item for the authenticated member.

This endpoint allows authenticated members to create a new todo task. The todo is automatically associated with the requesting member's account. Users must be authenticated via session token to create todos.

The created todo includes the following properties:
- A unique identifier assigned by the system
- The member ID automatically derived from the authenticated session
- The title provided in the request body
- An optional description explaining the task details
- Optional start and due dates for scheduling
- Completion status automatically set to false on creation
- Creation and update timestamps automatically recorded
- Soft-delete timestamp initially null

The system enforces ownership by associating the new todo with the authenticated user's member ID. Todos created through this endpoint are immediately visible in the user's todo list and are not marked as deleted.

This operation relates to other todo endpoints:
- GET /todos - List todos including the newly created one
- GET /todos/:id - View details of the created todo
- PATCH /todos/:id - Update properties of the created todo
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new todo record in the multi_user_todo_todos table.

1. Extract multi_user_todo_member_id from the authenticated session (from Authorization header or session cookie).

2. Validate request body:
   - title: Required, non-empty string
   - description: Optional, defaults to empty string
   - startDate: Optional, ISO 8601 date-time format
   - dueDate: Optional, ISO 8601 date-time format

3. Validate business rules:
   - Title must not be empty after trimming whitespace
   - If both startDate and dueDate are provided, dueDate must be after startDate

4. Insert into multi_user_todo_todos:
   - id: Generate new UUID
   - multi_user_todo_member_id: From authenticated session
   - title: From request body
   - description: From request body or empty string
   - start_date: From request body or null
   - due_date: From request body or null
   - completed: false (default)
   - created_at: Current timestamp
   - updated_at: Current timestamp
   - deleted_at: null

5. Return the created todo record with all fields populated.

responseBody.description: The newly created todo item with all properties

requestBody.description: Todo creation data including required title and optional description, startDate, and dueDate

operations.description:
Update an existing todo item with new values for editable fields.

This operation modifies the title, description, start date, and/or due date of a todo that the authenticated user owns. Any combination of these fields can be updated in a single request. The operation enforces strict ownership validation - users can only update todos they created.

The system validates that the target todo exists and is not in the trash (soft-deleted). If the todo is in trash, this operation returns an invalid state error since trash items must be restored before editing. When successful, the updated_at timestamp is automatically set to the current time.

This endpoint is typically used after retrieving a todo's details via GET /todos/{todoId} or listing todos via GET /todos. The response returns the complete updated todo object including all fields for client-side synchronization.

**Error Scenarios:**
- Returns 404 if the todo does not exist or belongs to another user
- Returns 400 if the todo is currently in trash (must be restored first)
- Validation errors for invalid field formats or business rule violations

**Related Operations:**
- GET /todos/{todoId} - Retrieve todo details before editing
- GET /todos - List all accessible todos
- POST /todos/{todoId}/restore - Restore a soft-deleted todo before updating
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update the multi_user_todo_todos record with the provided field values.

**Implementation Steps:**
1. Extract todoId from path parameters (UUID format)
2. Extract memberId from authenticated session
3. Query multi_user_todo_todos WHERE id = todoId AND multi_user_todo_member_id = memberId AND deleted_at IS NULL
4. If not found, return 404 error (todo not found or not owned by user)
5. Validate all provided fields against business rules:
   - title: required if provided, max length constraints
   - description: optional, string
   - start_date: optional, valid ISO 8601 timestamp
   - due_date: optional, valid ISO 8601 timestamp, must be after start_date if both provided
6. Update the record: set updated_at to CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, update provided fields
7. Return the complete updated todo record

**Transaction:** Single UPDATE query with WHERE clause including ownership check and deleted_at filter

responseBody.description: The complete updated todo entity with all fields

parameters.name: todoId

operations.description:
Soft delete a todo and move it to trash.

This operation marks a todo as deleted by setting the deleted_at timestamp to the current time. The todo is not physically removed from the database; instead, it is excluded from normal todo lists and moved to the trash.

The system verifies that the requesting member owns the todo before performing the deletion. If the todo does not belong to the requesting member, the operation returns a 403 Forbidden error.

The soft-delete operation preserves the entire edit history associated with the todo. Users can view deleted todos in the trash, restore them to active status, or permanently delete them.

After soft deletion, the todo will no longer appear in the active todo list (GET /todos) but will be visible in the trash (GET /trash). Users can restore a soft-deleted todo using POST /todos/{todoId}/restore.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Extract todoId from path parameter (UUID format)
2. Extract member_id from authenticated session (from JWT token)
3. Query multi_user_todo_todos table to find the todo by id
4. Verify the todo.multi_user_todo_member_id matches the authenticated member_id
5. If not found or ownership mismatch, return 404 Not Found or 403 Forbidden
6. Set todo.deleted_at to current timestamp (NOW())
7. Do NOT delete associated edit histories - they are preserved for potential restore
8. Return 204 No Content on success

Edge cases:
- Todo already deleted (deleted_at is not null): Return 404 Not Found (already in trash)
- Todo not found: Return 404 Not Found
- Unauthorized request: Return 401 Unauthorized

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo to soft-delete
parameters.name: todoId

prerequisites.description: Todo must exist before it can be soft-deleted. The POST operation creates the todo entity that will later be deleted via this endpoint.

operations.description:
Toggle the completion status of a todo between complete and incomplete.

This operation flips the completed flag on the target todo. When the todo is currently incomplete, this action marks it as complete. When the todo is currently complete, this action marks it as incomplete.

The operation only affects the completion status and does not modify any other fields. The updated_at timestamp is automatically updated to reflect the state change.

**Ownership Requirement**: The requesting member must own the todo. If the todo belongs to another user, the system returns a 403 Forbidden error.

**State Validation**: The todo must not be in the trash (deleted_at must be null). Attempting to toggle a deleted todo returns a 400 Bad Request error.

**Related Operations**:
- Use GET /todos/{todoId} to retrieve the todo before toggling
- Use GET /todos/{todoId}/history to view the edit history after toggling
- Use GET /todos to list all todos with their current completion status
operations.name: toggle
operations.specification:
1. Extract todoId from path parameters (UUID format)
2. Extract authenticated member ID from request context
3. Query multi_user_todo_todos table to find todo by id
4. Validate todo exists - return 404 if not found
5. Validate todo.deleted_at is null - return 400 if todo is in trash
6. Validate todo.multi_user_todo_member_id matches authenticated member ID - return 403 if ownership mismatch
7. Toggle the completed field: SET completed = NOT completed
8. Update updated_at timestamp to current time
9. Return the complete todo record with new completion status

responseBody.description: The updated todo with the toggled completion status

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo to toggle completion status
parameters.name: todoId

prerequisites.description: Todo must be created first before its completion status can be toggled. The toggle operation requires a specific todo by ID to exist in the database.

operations.description:
Restore a previously deleted todo from the trash back to the active todo list.

This endpoint allows authenticated users to recover their soft-deleted todos. When a todo is restored, its deleted_at timestamp is cleared, making it visible again in the normal todo list alongside non-deleted todos.

The restored todo maintains all its original data including title, description, start date, due date, and completion status. The edit history remains fully preserved and accessible.

This operation only succeeds when the todo exists and is currently in the trash (deleted_at is not null). Attempting to restore a todo that is not in the trash returns an error indicating the operation is invalid for the current state.

Ownership validation ensures users can only restore their own todos. The system enforces privacy isolation by rejecting restore requests for todos belonging to other users.

Related operations: Use DELETE /todos/{todoId} to move a todo to trash, GET /trash to view all deleted todos, and DELETE /trash/{todoId} for permanent deletion.
operations.name: restore
operations.specification:
Restore a soft-deleted todo from trash.

1. Authentication: Extract authenticated member ID from session/token.

2. Validate todoId parameter is a valid UUID format.

3. Query multi_user_todo_todos table:
   - Find todo by id
   - Verify multi_user_todo_member_id matches authenticated user
   - Verify deleted_at is NOT null (todo must be in trash)

4. If todo not found OR ownership mismatch OR deleted_at is null:
   - Return appropriate error response

5. Restore the todo by setting deleted_at to null and updating updated_at to current timestamp.

6. Return the restored todo entity with all fields including edit histories.

Transaction: Single UPDATE operation within transaction to ensure atomicity.

responseBody.description: The restored todo entity with all original data intact

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo to restore from trash
parameters.name: todoId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of soft-deleted todos for the authenticated member.

This endpoint returns all todos that have been moved to trash, allowing users to view their deleted items before deciding whether to restore or permanently delete them. The response is paginated with configurable page size and sorting options.

Each returned todo includes its title, description, dates, and completion status at the time of deletion. The timestamps indicate when the todo was originally created and when it was moved to trash.

Security: Only the authenticated member can access their own trash. Todos belonging to other users are not visible through this endpoint.

Related Operations:
- POST /todos/{id}/restore - Restore a specific todo from trash
- DELETE /todos/{id} - Soft delete a todo (moves to trash)
- DELETE /trash/{id} - Permanently delete a specific todo from trash
- DELETE /trash - Empty trash (permanently delete all items)

The trash list excludes active todos (those with null deleted_at). Users should first use GET /todos to view their active todo list.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query multi_user_todo_todos table filtering by multi_user_todo_member_id matching the authenticated session and deleted_at IS NOT NULL.

Query Parameters:
- page: Page number (default: 1, minimum: 1)
- limit: Items per page (default: 20, minimum: 1, maximum: 100)
- sortBy: Sort field - 'created_at', 'start_date', or 'due_date' (default: 'created_at')
- sortOrder: Sort direction - 'asc' or 'desc' (default: 'desc')

Business Rules:
- Only return todos where deleted_at is NOT NULL (soft-deleted items)
- Filter by multi_user_todo_member_id for privacy isolation
- Null handling for date sorting: todos without start_date/due_date appear at the end regardless of sort order
- No filtering by completion status (all deleted todos shown regardless of completion state)

Pagination Response:
Return paginated results with pagination metadata:
- items: Array of IMultiUserTodoTodos.ISummary
- total: Total count of deleted todos for the member
- page: Current page number
- limit: Items per page
- totalPages: Calculated total pages

Sort Order: ORDER BY {sortBy} {sortOrder}, NULLS LAST

No request body. Query parameters passed via URL query string.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of soft-deleted todo summaries

operations.description:
Permanently delete a todo from the trash.

This endpoint removes a todo that has been soft-deleted (moved to trash) and all its associated edit history entries from the system completely. The operation is irreversible and cannot be undone.

**Prerequisites**: The todo must already be in trash (soft-deleted with deleted_at timestamp set). Attempting to permanently delete an active todo returns an error.

**Scope**: The authenticated member can only permanently delete their own todos from trash. Accessing or deleting other users' todos is prohibited.

**Cascade Behavior**: When a todo is permanently deleted, the system also deletes all associated edit history entries (multi_user_todo_todo_edit_histories) via cascade delete.

**Response**: Returns 204 No Content on successful permanent deletion. Returns 404 Not Found if the todo does not exist or is not in trash.

**Related Operations**:
- POST /todos/{todoId} (restore) - Restore a todo from trash back to active list
- DELETE /todos/{todoId} - Soft-delete a todo (move to trash)
- GET /trash - View all todos in trash

Begin transaction, delete all associated edit history entries (cascade), then delete the todo record. Return 204 No Content on success. Handle errors: 404 if todo not found or not in trash, 403 if todo belongs to another user.

operations.description:
Retrieve the edit history of a specific todo with pagination and optional filtering.

This endpoint returns all edit history entries associated with the specified todo. Each history entry captures the changes made during a single edit operation, recording the old and new values for any fields that were modified (title, description, start date, due date).

History entries are displayed in reverse chronological order with the most recent edits appearing first. This allows users to quickly see the latest modifications to their todos.

Only active todos have accessible edit history. When a todo is moved to trash (soft-deleted), its history is not available for viewing. Once a todo is permanently deleted, all associated history entries are automatically removed as well.

Users can only view the edit history of their own todos. The system enforces ownership verification to ensure privacy and data isolation between users.

The response includes pagination metadata for navigating through large histories, along with summary information about each edit including the timestamp and the specific field changes that occurred.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query multi_user_todo_todo_edit_histories table filtered by multi_user_todo_todo_id matching the path parameter.

1. Ownership Verification:
   - First verify the todo exists in multi_user_todo_todos by todoId
   - Check that todo.multi_user_todo_member_id matches the authenticated user's member ID
   - Verify todo.deleted_at is null (active todo, not in trash)
   - If any check fails, return appropriate error response

2. History Query:
   - Query multi_user_todo_todo_edit_histories where multi_user_todo_todo_id = :todoId
   - Order by created_at DESC (newest first per requirements)
   - Apply pagination using page and limit parameters
   - Count total matching records for pagination metadata

3. Response Construction:
   - Map each history entry to ISummary format with:
     - id, created_at (timestamp of the edit)
     - old_title, new_title (null if not changed)
     - old_description, new_description (null if not changed)
     - old_start_date, new_start_date (null if not changed)
     - old_due_date, new_due_date (null if not changed)
   - Include pagination metadata: items, total, page, limit, totalPages

4. Error Handling:
   - 404 if todo not found
   - 403 if todo belongs to another user
   - 400 if todo is in trash (history not available for trashed todos)

operations.description:
Retrieve a single edit history entry for a todo.

This endpoint returns the details of a specific edit history entry associated with a todo. Each history entry records the changes made during a single edit operation, including the old and new values for any fields that were modified.

The history entry contains the timestamp when the edit was made, along with old/new values for title, description, start_date, and due_date. Fields that were not changed during that edit will have null values for both old and new.

**Security**: Only the owner of the todo can view its edit history. If the requesting user does not own the todo, the system returns a 404 error to maintain privacy.

**Todo Status**: Edit history is only available for active todos. If the specified todo has been moved to trash (deleted_at is not null), the system returns a 404 error indicating that history is not available for trashed todos.

**Relationship to Todo**: The history entry is linked to its parent todo through the multi_user_todo_todo_id field. This endpoint requires both the todo ID and history ID to ensure precise retrieval of the specific history entry.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
1. Extract todoId and historyId from path parameters.
2. Query multi_user_todo_todos table to find the todo by todoId.
3. Verify the todo exists - return 404 if not found.
4. Verify the todo's multi_user_todo_member_id matches the authenticated user's member ID - return 404 if not authorized (do not reveal existence to unauthorized users).
5. Verify the todo's deleted_at is null - return 404 if the todo is in trash (history not available for trashed todos).
6. Query multi_user_todo_todo_edit_histories table to find the history entry by historyId.
7. Verify the history entry's multi_user_todo_todo_id matches the todoId - return 404 if not found.
8. Return the history entry with all fields: id, todo_id, created_at, old_title, new_title, old_description, new_description, old_start_date, new_start_date, old_due_date, new_due_date.
9. The completion status of a todo is NOT tracked in the edit history.

IMultiUserTodoTodo.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Request DTO for querying multi_user_todo_todos with filters and pagination. Source: multi_user_todo_todos table filtered by authenticated member_id. Filters: status maps to completed column ('all'=no filter, 'complete'=true, 'incomplete'=false), date range filters map to start_date and due_date columns with >= and <= comparisons. Sorting: sortBy maps to created_at/start_date/due_date columns with NULLS LAST for nullable columns. Pagination: Skip (page - 1) * limit records. Excludes soft-deleted todos (WHERE deleted_at IS NULL).
